features.note: Opaque architecture captures keep the front public band, center circulation spine, paired room masses and rear strip readable while shell, roof, glass and floor zones remain separated.

The floor-comparison and corridor captures preserve stepped room/floor separation and clearly isolate dark matte carpet from the brighter circulation finish; later family-owned upholstery and acoustic finish polish is not required at this shell gate.
The facade reads as a coherent red, charcoal, warm-white and glazed public threshold, although several individual PBR responses remain too flat.
Across the engineering captures, green solid routes and blue dashed/segmented media remain separable against the translucent shell, with endpoint labels readable at the closer view.
The architecture set is opaque and mass-led, while the engineering set is clearly translucent and exposes zone volumes, labels and media without an apparent geometry change.

important_features.note: People, entrance doors, room openings and engineering markers retain a coherent relative scale in the facade and overview captures.
Bright public finishes and red/white accents separate from the dark carpeted circulation bands without relying on final lighting, though the look-dev exposure compresses material highlights.
Green and blue routes remain visually contained and traceable through the transparent engineering shell at overview and corridor scales.

defects: In the neutral and grazing architecture captures, exterior concrete and warm-white coated walls are distinguished mostly by base value; both retain broad, nearly uniform fields with too little visible roughness or micro-normal separation.

The red facade metal stays uniformly saturated through neutral, grazing and facade views, with little soft clearcoat highlight rolloff, so it reads closer to flat plastic or emissive color than painted dielectric metal.
Facade glazing reads as milky pale blue-gray infill rather than clearly transmissive glass; the charcoal mullions are distinct, but interior silhouettes or environmental transmission cues are weak.
The floor-comparison view proves a light public-floor versus dark carpet boundary, but the public tile does not show a convincing broad glossy reflection or highlight while the carpet remains matte.
The grazing facade view is too washed in the white and light-gray range to serve as strong diagnostic evidence for the specified concrete-versus-coating response.
corrections: Run a Material Realism Reset limited to response: give concrete visibly broader, broken matte response and coated warm-white walls a smoother, tighter highlight, then save neutral and grazing captures where both finishes are simultaneously readable without changing their geometry or adding graphics.

Make the red facade trim produce a restrained clearcoat lobe with visible highlight rolloff instead of a uniformly bright red strip; preserve its dielectric painted-metal identity and avoid emissive-looking saturation.

Increase visible transmission and environmental contrast in the facade panes so background or interior silhouettes can be seen through the blue-gray glass while keeping every charcoal mullion fully opaque.

Strengthen the public tile's broad low-roughness reflection in the floor-comparison capture while keeping the corridor carpet reflection-free and visibly matte; do not add decorative patterns or surface graphics.

Rebalance only the look-dev grazing exposure or light angle so light concrete, coated wall and red clearcoat highlights are not clipped; do not substitute final architectural lighting for material proof.

mechanical.note: Nine attempt-2 capture sidecars report no console, page, warning or network issues. Probe reports 164 draws and 22344 triangles within the 550-draw and 750000-triangle budgets; fps is informational only under SwiftShader.
